records.name: Friends of Fitler Square Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Fitler Square Park, a small park on Pine Street between 23rd and 24th Streets. They run a summer concert series, a fall fundraiser, and an annual spring event, and they recruit volunteers and committee members.
records.what_you_do: Help at the two park cleanups each year, or join one of four committees: communications, events, fundraising, or grounds upkeep. Donations and bench adoptions also support the park.

schedule.text: Summer concerts in the park run 6 to 8 pm. The group also holds a fall fundraiser and an annual spring event.

cost.text: Summer concerts list no admission cost. The fall fundraiser is ticketed; its page gives no ticket price and says the event has sold out.

first_step.how: Come to a summer concert in the park, then fill out the Committee Interest Form on the group's committees page, or email friendsoffitlersquarepark@gmail.com to ask about the next cleanup.
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to the public, and the volunteer page explains the cleanup sign-up and the committee form, though it gives no set meeting times.
first_step.what_to_expect: Concerts run from 6 to 8 pm and feature live bands. The bands listed on the events page play blues, folk, bluegrass, and Irish tunes. The fall fundraiser is an evening of dinner, drinks, and music for people 21 and older.
first_visit_tips: Each concert has a listed rain date, so check the events page if the weather looks bad.
Cleanup sign-up forms are posted shortly before each cleanup, so watch the volunteer page before a cleanup date.

records.notes: Last sign of life moved from 2026-10 to 2026-09. Tier 1 used the city list check date. The newest dated item the group publishes is the Friday, September 18 fundraiser. That page gives the day and not the year; 2026 comes from the events calendar, which sits under an October 2026 heading. Summer concerts were on July 10 and August 7 with rain dates listed. The volunteer page's board email link points to a different address (FSIA1962@gmail.com) than the one shown; the displayed address is used and the owner should confirm it. The Saturday farmers market mentioned on the fundraiser page is not presented as a volunteer shift, so it is left out. No accessibility details on the site. No nearest SEPTA recorded.

records.name: Friends of Gold Star Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Gold Star Park, a small park on Wharton Street in South Philadelphia. They run programs for kids, families, and dog owners, and they invite new volunteers to help.
records.what_you_do: Help run the park's summer programs and its upkeep. The site does not describe volunteer tasks in detail.

schedule.text: Children's, family, and dog-owner programs run through the summer; no dates are published on the group's site.

first_step.how: Sign up for the group's newsletter at goldstarpark.org, or message the group on its Facebook page, and ask how to volunteer.
first_step.basis: The site invites new volunteers and offers a newsletter sign-up, though it publishes no meeting schedule.
first_step.what_to_expect: The group does not publish meeting times or program dates, so ask before you come. The park already has morning tai chi, a bocce league, and a daily stop for neighborhood dogs. The group's summer programs are for kids, families, and dog owners.
first_visit_tips: Check the newsletter or the group's Facebook page for the next program date.
Ask how to volunteer before you come, since the site does not describe volunteer tasks in detail.

records.notes: The site has no volunteer or membership page, so the first step relies on the newsletter sign-up and the Facebook page. The group's own email is hidden behind a link on its site and could not be read, so the record keeps the City stewardship office address from the city list. Status moved from active to probably_active: the site works but shows no dated items. The tier 1 last sign of life of 2026-10 was the city list check date, so it is cleared. Instagram and Twitter links come from the site footer. No accessibility details on the site. No nearest SEPTA recorded.

records.name: Friends of Gorgas Park
records.summary: Neighbors who care for Gorgas Park in Roxborough. They put on park concerts and family events, and they hold spring planting and cleanup days.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a spring planting or cleanup day, help at a family event or concert, or donate to the park. The group also runs a garden club that meets weekly; the site does not say how to join it.

schedule.text: Spring planting and cleanup days, and summer concerts. Dates are posted each season on the group's site.

cost.text: No admission or membership fee listed; the site has a donate page

first_step.how: Watch the Volunteer Opportunities page on gorgaspark.com for the next spring planting or cleanup day, and sign up through the link posted there.
first_step.basis: Planting and cleanup days are open to volunteers who sign up on the group's site. The site does not describe a first-timer step.
first_step.what_to_expect: Spring planting and cleanup days are the main way to help, and they are announced each season. The site does not say how long these days last, what tasks there are, or what to bring. A past planting day had limited spots, so sign up early.
first_visit_tips: Sign up early, since a past planting day had limited spots.
The site does not list what to bring or wear. The Contact Us form on gorgaspark.com is the only listed way to ask.

records.notes: Last sign of life corrected from 2026-10 to 2026-06. The newest dated item the group publishes is a June 23, 2026 post with a photo and no event details. Tier 1's 2026-10 came from the city list check date. No dated events after October 8, 2026 were found. The volunteer page mentions a weekly garden club run by the group, but gives no name, day, time, or way to join; it is mentioned in what_you_do only. The contact page has a form and no published email or phone, so the City stewardship email from tier 1 is kept. The contact name John J Boyce is carried from tier 1 IRS and city records and does not appear on the site. No accessibility details on the site.

records.name: Friends of Harrowgate Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Harrowgate Park in Kensington. They put on park events such as a movie night and a winter tree lighting, and they take part in neighborhood art projects.
records.what_you_do: Come to park events, donate through the site, or ask how to help with the next event. The site does not describe volunteer tasks.

schedule.text: Community events at the park, such as a movie night and a winter tree lighting. Check the events page for dates.

cost.text: No admission or dues listed for events. The site has a donate page with no suggested amount.

first_step.how: Come to the Friends of Harrowgate Park Movie Night on October 16, 2026 at the park, 3455 Kensington Ave, from 4 pm, and ask a Friends member how to help.
first_step.basis: Events are open to the public on set dates. The site does not explain how to join the group or volunteer.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Movie Night runs 3:30 to 8 pm. Activities start at 4 pm, with a DJ, refreshments, arts and crafts, face painting, balloon twisters, and a game truck, and the film starts at 6 pm. Bring your own blanket or chairs. The event page does not list an admission price.
first_visit_tips: Bring your own blanket or chairs, as the event page asks.
Plan to arrive by 4 pm for the activities; the movie starts at 6 pm.
The site has no accessibility details, so call (215) 683-3600 or email the group before you come if you need access help.

records.notes: The Fall Festival (October 10) and Winter Festival (December 12) on the events page are run by Harrowgate Civic, a separate group, so they are not on this record. Harrowgate Civic is in leads_only. Schedule text names no dates; dated items sit in first_step and last_sign_of_life. The Movie Night time and activities come from its own event page. The contact page names no person; the contact name Sonja Bingham is carried from tier 1 city and IRS records and is not on the site. Friday fits both listed dates (October 16 and December 11, 2026). The site has no accessibility, parking, or transit details, so none are recorded and no nearest SEPTA is named.

records.name: Friends of FDR Park
records.summary: A nonprofit that supports South Philadelphia's largest park. It backs park programs and local wildlife and works toward a long-term park plan.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on Saturday mornings or at the Welcome Center desk, join as a member (membership starts at $25), or donate. The group says donations go to the park.

schedule.text: Regular volunteer hours are Saturdays, 10 am to 12 pm. Welcome Center desk shifts run daily, 9 am to 4 pm. Events are posted on the group's calendar. The park is open daily: 6 am to 9 pm from April to October, and 6 am to 6 pm from November to March.

cost.text: Membership starts at $25. Group or corporate volunteer days require a yearly membership of $200 or $500. Donations are optional.

access.notes: Two restrooms: one outside the Welcome Center at 1800 Pattison Ave, and one across from the skatepark, under I-95.

first_step.how: Fill out the general volunteer sign-up form on the Volunteer page of fdrparkphilly.org. You will then get a monthly newsletter with sign-up links for park work.
first_step.basis: The site gives a clear sign-up route and a first-day orientation for Welcome Center volunteers, but it does not say beginners are specially welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Regular volunteer sessions run Saturdays from 10 am to 12 pm, and Welcome Center desk shifts run up to seven hours. Welcome Center volunteers get an orientation on their first day. Group and corporate volunteer days need a yearly membership.
first_visit_tips: The Welcome Center is at 1800 Pattison Ave, and there is a restroom outside it.
For a desk shift, sign up through the shift spreadsheet linked on the volunteer page.
If you need community service hours, email stewardship@fdrpark.org.

records.notes: Membership pricing: the membership page lists a $25 starting price but no named levels, and the $200 and $500 yearly levels come from the volunteer page. Status moved from active to probably_active: the site works, but no dated items were on the pages read. The tier 1 last sign of life of 2026-10 was the city list check date, so it is cleared. The volunteer page has a Leaf and Learn toddler program (ages 2 to 5) and a Bark Ambassadors program; they are not in this record. No nearest SEPTA recorded.
